title: What Is AWS and Cloud Computing?

options.text: On-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing
A single piece of software you install on one laptop
Buying and owning servers for your own data center
A programming language for building websites

questions.explanation: Cloud computing is the on-demand delivery of compute, storage, databases, and networking over the internet, billed pay-as-you-go — not a single product or owned hardware.

questions.prompt: Match each service model to what it provides.

pairs.right: Raw infrastructure like virtual servers; you manage the OS (e.g., Amazon EC2)
A managed platform so you focus on your code (e.g., Elastic Beanstalk)
Finished software you just use in a browser

questions.explanation: IaaS gives building blocks you manage, PaaS manages the servers/OS for you, and SaaS is complete software you simply use.

questions.prompt: Order the service models from the one where YOU manage the MOST to the one where you manage the LEAST.
questions.explanation: With IaaS you manage the most (OS and up); PaaS hands the servers/OS to the provider; with SaaS you manage the least — you just use the app.

questions.prompt: Which of these are genuine benefits of the cloud model as described in the lesson? Select all that apply.

options.text: Trade capital expense (CapEx) for variable expense (OpEx)
Stop guessing capacity by scaling up and down with demand
It is always cheaper than on-premises no matter how you use it
Provision resources on demand in minutes rather than buying hardware

questions.explanation: The cloud trades CapEx for OpEx, removes the capacity guess through elasticity, and provisions in minutes. It is NOT automatically cheaper — savings require right-sizing and turning off idle resources.

questions.prompt: The service model that gives you virtual servers where you control the operating system is abbreviated ____ (four letters).
questions.explanation: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) provides raw infrastructure such as Amazon EC2 virtual servers, where you manage the OS and everything above it.

questions.prompt: Why is moving a workload to AWS not automatically cheaper?

options.text: AWS charges a fixed monthly fee regardless of usage
Savings come from elasticity and right-sizing; an oversized, always-on resource just relocates the waste
The cloud can only run small workloads
You must buy hardware up front on AWS too

questions.explanation: Pay-as-you-go rewards efficiency. If you move an oversized server and never turn it off, you carry the same waste — cost savings depend on right-sizing and shutting down idle resources.
